newsitem.title: USA: Dow at record ahead of Fed meet, Intel hits Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Dow at record ahead of Fed meet, Intel hits Nasdaq.

text.p: The Dow industrials edged to another record high as bonds rallied amid expectations the Fed will stand pat on interest rates Wednesday, but the Nasdaq Composite was beset by late selling in Intel and other techs.

"We don't expect any changes from the Fed. The economic picture is almost perfectly mixed. We have middle-of-the-road politics, mediocre economic growth and low interest rates. We also don't expect surprises on inflation," said Barbara Marcin, a vice president at Citibank Global Asset Management.
The Dow rose 10 to about 6266, its fifth straight record.
It was the longest string of Dow records since the seven-session streak from February 5-13.

The long bond soared 26/32 to yield 6.45 percent, a fresh eight-month low. Treasury prices surged on optimism that bipartisan cooperation could lead to a resolution on a balanced U.S. budget, expectations of no change in monetary policy at Wednesday's FOMC meeting and still-benign inflation numbers Wednesday and Thursday.
The S&P 500 fell two to about 730, snapping its five-session record streak. The-tech studded Nasdaq Composite lost six to about 1257 after scoring a new record on Monday.

Bellwether Intel, which earlier hit a fresh 52-week high 125-1/8 after bullish book-to-bill data, lost 2-7/8 to 121. Intel reversed course as traders interpreted a Goldman Sachs call to clients as a caution that personal computer sales may be slowing. A Goldman spokesman denied the brokerage had downgraded Intel or any of the PC manufacturing stocks.

Analysts said technology stocks were also pressured by Microsoft chairman Bill Gates' comments that an array of companies supporting the network computer movement posed the stiffest challenge the software giant has seen in years.
Microsoft lost 1-7/8 to 141-3/4.

Among other tech stocks, Micron fell 1-1/4 to 30-5/8, LSI Logic lost 1-1/8 to 31-1/8, Compaq shed 2-3/4 to 73-1/2, Dell Computer was off 1-3/4 to 88-5/8 and IBM fell 1-3/8 to 133-1/8. But Motorola was up 1-7/8 to 51-7/8.
Chip stocks were initially buoyed by news that the October book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.10, beating even the rosiest expectations. But afternoon profit-taking ensued.
"The market was in a mood to find an excuse for profit-taking. It's had an awfully nice run and traders are getting itchy here," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist.
Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities analyst, said, "The book to bill was great but techs ran ahead of themselves and this afternoon they decided to take profits."

"The market has run out of steam," Zagorski said, adding that Wall Street was not expecting any negative news from Wednesday's Fed meeting or October producer prices or Thursday's consumer prices report.
Among individual issues, Wal-mart lost 1-1/4 to 25-1/4 after reporting third-quarter share earnings rose to $0.30, missing the Street's consensus by one penny.
Westinghouse rose 5/8 to 20-5/8.
The company declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal report that it plans to spin off its industrial businesses into a separate company.
AT&T rose 1-1/4 to 38-3/8. The U.S. Supreme Court declined a request by federal regulators to reactivate rules meant to pry open U.S. local phone monopolies to competition.

Home Depot slumped 3-3/8 to 53-3/8 after reporting in-line quarterly results. Industry analysts said some investors had hoped for an even better quarter, while other investors worried about a possible peaking in the housing market.
Informix lost three to 17-5/8.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette trimmed fourth-quarter earnings estimates and fiscal 1997 estimates based on heightened market competition.

Anchor Gaming slumped 8-7/8 to 30-1/8 after news it is "re-evaluating" plans for expanding a Colorado casino. Analysts said investors were surprised by the news and the company's statement left the market with more questions than answers about Anchor's growth strategy.
Gold mining stocks were firmer despite expectations inflation will remain benign. Newmont Mining rose 1-1/8 to 50-5/8 and Battle Mountain Gold rose 3/8 to 8-3/8.

Interest-rate sensitive issues rose as the long bond yield headed lower. Citicorp rose one to 102-3/8, Merrill Lynch rose 1/4 to 77, AMR Corp was up 2-5/8 to 88-5/8, General Re added 2-1/8 to 157-3/8 and Delta Air rose 1-7/8 to 77-1/4.
Winners beat losers 1325 to 1102 on very heavy NYSE volume of 471.7 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.14 to 1256.53.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.31 to 729.56.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
